defaultInterfaceClaim.notes: Every generated declaration starts unreviewed. Promote an overload only with an explicit ID override: positive claims require executable evidence, while negative, excluded, or deferred claims require an owned rationale.

interfaceOverrides.notes: Task.cancel() routes to the runtime handle; same-source probes cover cancellation before execution and cancellation observed by a running operation.
The active-SDK escalatePriority(to:) signature is retained, but explicit handle-priority mutation has no runtime intrinsic and fails with the generated-surface diagnostic.
The deprecated async nonthrowing get() overload is inventoried separately from value, but name-level runtime dispatch currently diagnoses it instead of silently aliasing it.
The deprecated async throwing get() overload is retained with its throwing effect, but name-level runtime dispatch currently diagnoses it instead of silently aliasing it.
The deprecated async getResult() signature is generated, but runtime member lookup diagnoses it rather than claiming an unverified alias to result.
Task.hash(into:) is present in the generated denominator, while RuntimeTaskHandle has no source-visible Hashable bridge and reports an explicit unsupported diagnostic.
Task.hashValue is inventoried but RuntimeTaskHandle does not expose source-level Hashable semantics; lookup fails explicitly instead of returning an incidental host hash.
Task.isCancelled reads the runtime handle's cancellation record; same-source probes distinguish target-handle state from waiter cancellation.
The async result property suspends on the runtime handle and preserves success, failure, cancellation, and repeated terminal reads without throwing from the property access.
The async nonthrowing value overload waits for and reproduces the stored successful outcome, including repeated reads after completion.
The async throwing value overload waits for the runtime handle and rethrows its stored source failure with native-parity repeated-outcome behavior.
Task handle equality is retained in the generated static denominator, but RuntimeTaskHandle does not yet expose source Equatable identity and the operator fails explicitly.
The deprecated Task.CancellationError() compatibility spelling is inventoried but is not aliased by the runtime and receives the generated unsupported diagnostic.
Task.basePriority is generated but source lookup does not expose the runtime record's base priority and fails explicitly.
Task.checkCancellation() throws from a cancelled source task and remains nonthrowing for an active task; same-source group probes exercise the cancelled path.
Task.currentPriority reads the task-owned effective priority; native-parity probes cover inheritance and direct and transitive donation.

Nonthrowing detached execution, priority, value, and task-owned name semantics have same-source evidence for the supported nonisolated subset; the complete @isolated(any) operation executor contract remains divergent.
Throwing detached execution, failure propagation, and task-owned name storage work through the shared runtime path; the complete @isolated(any) operation executor contract remains divergent.
The nonthrowing executorPreference detached overload is preserved, while custom task executors are outside the runtime contract and receive a shape-specific diagnostic.
The throwing executorPreference detached overload is separately inventoried, while custom task executors are outside the runtime contract and receive a shape-specific diagnostic.
Static Task.isCancelled reads the current source task rather than a handle; same-source probes cover inherited cancellation and cancellation isolation.

Task.name reads the immutable name of the current logical runtime task. Same-source Swift 6 parity covers an unnamed root, named ordinary and detached tasks, nonnil and explicit-nil optional arguments, non-inheritance into an unnamed child, preservation of an empty string, and named plus unnamed task-group children.
The deprecated nonthrowing runDetached overload retains its actor-context metadata but has no runtime compatibility alias and is diagnosed.
The deprecated throwing runDetached overload is retained separately but has no runtime compatibility alias and is diagnosed.
The deprecated positional nonthrowing sleep suspends and records cancellation without throwing; the unchanged swiftlang cancellation-handler fixture proves the effect distinction.
Task.sleep(for:) supports Duration and cancellation with the default continuous clock, but explicit tolerance and generic clock arguments are currently ignored.
The generic deadline-based sleep overload is retained, but source clock instants are not modeled and the call fails explicitly.
Task.sleep(nanoseconds:) creates a first-class sleeping suspension and throws CancellationError when the source task is cancelled.
The deprecated Task.suspend() spelling is retained but is not silently redirected to yield and receives the generated unsupported diagnostic.
The deprecated Task.withCancellationHandler spelling is inventoried, while only the modern top-level API is implemented and the legacy member is diagnosed.
The deprecated Task.withGroup spelling is inventoried, while modern task-group entry points are implemented separately and the legacy member is diagnosed.
Task.yield() records a first-class yielding suspension and permits another ready source task to make progress without asserting scheduler order.
DiscardingTaskGroup.isCancelled reads the group's combined cancellation state; the same-source four-kind probe proves the active-to-cancelled transition around cancelAll.
DiscardingTaskGroup.isEmpty becomes false for an outstanding child and true after automatic outcome consumption; the same-source probe waits for the cancelled child to drain.
TaskGroup.isCancelled is false initially and true immediately after cancelAll; two same-source probes cover the transition with and without a child.
TaskGroup.isEmpty tracks unconsumed outcomes. The same-source four-kind probe and unchanged swiftlang async_taskgroup_is_empty.swift both cover empty, outstanding, and drained states.
ThrowingDiscardingTaskGroup.isCancelled reads the group's combined cancellation state; the same-source four-kind probe proves the active-to-cancelled transition around cancelAll.
ThrowingDiscardingTaskGroup.isEmpty becomes false for an outstanding child and true after automatic outcome consumption; the probe catches the child's cancellation before draining.
ThrowingTaskGroup.isCancelled is false initially and true after cancelAll in the same-source four-kind state probe.
ThrowingTaskGroup.isEmpty tracks the outstanding child until try await next consumes its successful outcome in the same-source four-kind probe.
DiscardingTaskGroup.cancelAll() requests cancellation of its outstanding child; the four-kind same-source probe observes cancellation, waits for automatic consumption, and exits empty.
TaskGroup.cancelAll() cancels outstanding children without cancelling the owner and scope exit still joins them; repository and unchanged swiftlang same-source probes cover both rules.
ThrowingDiscardingTaskGroup.cancelAll() requests cancellation without manufacturing a body error; the caught child cancellation is automatically consumed before empty scope exit.
ThrowingTaskGroup.cancelAll() requests child cancellation while preserving a successful caught child outcome that remains consumable through try await next().

Default and explicit MainActor.shared TaskGroup.waitForAll calls have native parity for joining, consumption, suspension, and MainActor resumption. The complete any-Actor contract remains a known divergence until arbitrary actor executors are modeled.

Default and explicit MainActor.shared ThrowingTaskGroup.waitForAll calls have native parity for success, drain, failure, cancellation, suspension, and MainActor resumption. The complete any-Actor contract remains a known divergence until arbitrary actor executors are modeled.

ThrowingTaskGroup.nextResult has native parity for empty, success, source failure, cancellation, single consumption, and explicit MainActor resumption. The complete any-Actor contract remains a known divergence until arbitrary actor executors are modeled.

Deprecated TaskGroup.spawn(priority:operation:) routes through the ordinary group-child primitive. Same-source parity passes an explicit priority and covers unconditional value delivery without claiming exact effective priority; unchanged swiftlang coverage adds repeated default-priority children drained by async iteration.

Deprecated ThrowingTaskGroup.spawn(priority:operation:) routes through the throwing group-child primitive. Same-source parity passes an explicit priority and covers unconditional value delivery plus source-error projection without claiming exact effective priority; unchanged swiftlang coverage adds repeated successful children drained by throwing async iteration.

Deprecated TaskGroup.async(priority:operation:) routes through the ordinary group-child primitive. Same-source parity passes an explicit priority and covers unconditional value delivery without claiming exact effective priority; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently exercises the default-priority spelling and group state transition.

Deprecated ThrowingTaskGroup.async(priority:operation:) routes through the throwing group-child primitive. Same-source parity passes an explicit priority and covers unconditional value delivery plus source-error projection through next() without claiming exact effective priority.

Deprecated async TaskGroup.add(priority:operation:) is generated from the active SDK body that forwards to addTaskUnlessCancelled. Same-source parity covers accepted value delivery before cancellation and false with no child after cancelAll; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently anchors the shared cancellation primitive.

Deprecated async ThrowingTaskGroup.add(priority:operation:) is generated from the active SDK body that forwards to addTaskUnlessCancelled. Same-source parity covers accepted success, exact child-error projection, and false with no child after cancelAll; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently anchors the shared cancellation primitive.

Deprecated TaskGroup.asyncUnlessCancelled(priority:operation:) forwards to the generated addTaskUnlessCancelled intrinsic. Same-source parity covers synchronous true/value before cancellation and false with no child after cancelAll; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently anchors rejection by the shared modern primitive.

Deprecated ThrowingTaskGroup.asyncUnlessCancelled(priority:operation:) forwards to the generated addTaskUnlessCancelled intrinsic. Same-source parity covers synchronous true, success and exact source-error delivery, then false with no child after cancelAll; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently anchors rejection by the shared modern primitive.

Deprecated TaskGroup.spawnUnlessCancelled(priority:operation:) forwards to the generated addTaskUnlessCancelled intrinsic. The unchanged pinned swiftlang cancel-then-spawn fixture directly proves true/value before cancellation, false/empty after cancelAll, and the contrast with unconditional spawn creating an already-cancelled child.

Deprecated ThrowingTaskGroup.spawnUnlessCancelled(priority:operation:) forwards to the generated addTaskUnlessCancelled intrinsic. Same-source parity covers true with success and exact source-error delivery, then false with no child after cancelAll; the pinned ordinary swiftlang fixture independently exercises the sibling alias.

TaskGroup.makeAsyncIterator returns a distinct iterator capability over the group's shared completion stream. Same-source parity covers explicit MainActor-isolated next calls, order-independent value consumption, and nil after exhaustion; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently drains an ordinary group through async iteration.

ThrowingTaskGroup.makeAsyncIterator returns a distinct iterator capability over the group's shared completion stream. Same-source parity covers default success, explicit MainActor source-error projection, and terminal nil after that error; unchanged swiftlang coverage independently drains a throwing group through async iteration.
TaskGroup.Iterator.cancel() permanently finishes that iterator value, requests cancellation of the shared group, and causes addTaskUnlessCancelled to reject new work in the same-source probe.

The non-isolated TaskGroup.Iterator.next() overload consumes the shared completion queue exactly once. Same-source parity covers success, terminal nil across later group work, and value-semantic iterator-copy independence.

Explicit MainActor.shared TaskGroup.Iterator.next calls have native parity for shared consumption, terminal state, and copy independence. The complete isolated any-Actor contract remains a known divergence until arbitrary actor executors are modeled.
ThrowingTaskGroup.Iterator.cancel() permanently finishes that iterator value, requests cancellation of the shared group, and causes addTaskUnlessCancelled to reject new work in the same-source probe.

The non-isolated ThrowingTaskGroup.Iterator.next() overload preserves successful values and exact source-error projection. A thrown child permanently finishes that iterator while leaving later work consumable through the group.

Explicit MainActor.shared ThrowingTaskGroup.Iterator.next calls have native parity for source-error projection and terminal state. The complete isolated any-Actor contract remains a known divergence until arbitrary actor executors are modeled.

A local protocol requirement forces Swift to select the @_disfavoredOverload TaskGroup.next() compatibility witness. Same-source parity covers empty, success, exactly-once drain, cancellation state, and an unconditionally added child observing cancellation.

A local protocol requirement forces Swift to select the @_disfavoredOverload ThrowingTaskGroup.next() compatibility witness. Same-source parity covers empty, success, exact source-error recovery, cancellation projection, and terminal drain.

Swift resolves direct group.next() source to the modern defaulted-isolation overload. Default, nonisolated explicit-nil, and explicit MainActor.shared calls have native parity for empty, success, drain, cancellation, and resumption; arbitrary source-defined actor executors remain a known divergence.

Swift resolves direct group.next() source to the modern defaulted-isolation overload. Default, nonisolated explicit-nil, and explicit MainActor.shared calls have native parity for empty, success, source failure, recovery, cancellation, drain, and resumption; arbitrary source-defined actor executors remain a known divergence.

The deprecated nonthrowing top-level async overload routes through the ordinary unstructured-task runtime. Same-source Swift 6 evidence covers inherited MainActor execution, explicit priority, unnamed task metadata, lifetime beyond the creating function, and successful value delivery for that supported subset; the complete @isolated(any) operation executor contract remains divergent until arbitrary actor executors are modeled.

Its default-isolation subset has native parity for active, pre-cancelled, nested, throwing, and scope-exit behavior; an explicitly supplied isolation is diagnosed until arbitrary source actor executors and resume ownership exist.

semanticCapabilities.notes: Basic async function execution and await have a same-source differential oracle; richer suspension and ownership families are accounted separately.
Source tasks own evaluator context and explicitly rebind it on detached host re-entry.
Task values, failures, cancellation state, waiters, detached work, and handle lifetime have native parity.
Suspension, sleep, yield, and cancellation-handler semantics are covered.
Async-let values, failure, cancellation, lexical cleanup, and diagnostics are covered.
The covered core includes joining, result consumption, cancellation, nested ownership, and cleanup.
Core semantics exist, but every generated overload still needs an explicit implementation/verification disposition.
Logical MainActor/default-executor hops are covered without claiming physical parallelism.
Valid actor declarations can still enter class-like execution; the next cycle begins by making unsupported actor semantics fail closed.
Actor-owned identity/storage and serial mailbox/executor queues are not implemented.
Actor reentrancy/resume ownership, isolated dispatch, arbitrary global actors, and mailbox stress are not implemented.
The native compiler supplies isolation and pinned concurrency diagnostics before interpreter mutation, including MainActor inheritance from an imported or synthetic nominal type.
Pinned upstream Sendable diagnostics are delegated to production compiler preflight; no independent interpreter type checker is claimed.
Protocol iteration, streams, and continuation ownership wait for M5 executor/resume ownership.
View identity, cancellation, and teardown semantics remain behind M5 and M7.
Physical worker execution and Thread Sanitizer evidence are intentionally deferred until ownership and isolation stabilize.
